He has a strong work ethic and already takes calculated risks. The rule "If strong work ethic then (success XOR risks)" (both not allowed) forces Arjun not to achieve success.

Thus Arjun: (i) finishes ahead of schedule, (ii) mentors others.

The last conditional says: If (ahead AND mentor) then Arjun is NOT an effective leader. Both antecedents hold, so by modus ponens Arjun is not an effective leader.

Therefore the statement "Arjun is an effective leader." is entailed false.
